children: Swarmer has signed a memorandum of understanding with Vectus Air Defense Systems to build and deploy air defense systems in eligible markets.

Under the nonbinding MOU, Vectus said it intends to purchase and deploy at least 40 of the systems in the first year after production and at least 80 in the second year. The systems are expected to be priced between $5 million and $6 million, Swarmer U.S. Chief Executive Officer Alex Fink said. Swarmer holds a 20% stake in Vectus.
The drone company said Wednesday it intends to build a manufacturing facility for the new systems in Poland.

"We intend to manufacture an end-to-end solution that includes radars, cameras, fire control and effectors to target a variety of threats, including newer jet-powered Shahed-type attack drones," Fink said. "The systems use combat-proven Gatling-type rotary cannons, capable of firing 20mm rounds at a rate of up to 6,000 rounds per minute, as the last line of defense."
